appraisal_events.evidence: quand la duchesse venait dîner, la princesse se gardait bien d'avoir ses habitués et fermait sa porte... la princesse de Parme admettait fort bien qu'on pût se plaire davantage dans la société de Mme de Guermantes que dans la sienne propre... elle n'avait qu'une peur, c'était de ne pas savoir comprendre, retenir, plaire.
appraisal_events.explanation: The princesse de Parme organizes her own household around the duchesse's presence, concedes that society prefers Oriane's company to her own, and is anxious above all to please and measure up when dining with her, a sustained deference to the duchesse's superior social and personal authority.

appraisal_events.evidence: quand Swann jugeait Brichot et Elstir, l'un comme un pédant, l'autre comme un mufle, malgré tout le savoir de l'un et tout le génie de l'autre, c'était l'infiltration de l'esprit Guermantes qui l'avait fait les classer ainsi.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator exposes Swann's harsh private verdicts on Brichot and Elstir as not his own true judgment but the product of an absorbed, hollow snobbish code, diminishing Swann by revealing the compromised source of his discernment.

status_effects.explanation: A sovereign princess restructures her own receptions around the duchesse's visits and openly concedes that society prefers Oriane's company to her own, a clear witnessed mark of the duchesse's superior standing.
Despite her rank, the princesse de Parme is anxious and dependent when in the duchesse's orbit, fearing above all that she will fail to understand, retain, or please Oriane.
Swann is shown to have internalized the hollow 'esprit des Guermantes,' leading him to dismiss real learning and genius out of borrowed snobbery rather than independent judgment.
Despite Swann's dismissive label of pedant, the narrator credits Brichot with real learning, a backhanded affirmation set against Swann's snobbish verdict.
Despite Swann's dismissive label of boor, the narrator credits Elstir with real genius, a backhanded affirmation set against Swann's snobbish verdict.
